properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Loddon River Laanecoorie to Loddon Weir.

  • Minor flooding is occurring at Laanecoorie Reservoir.
  • The Loddon River at Laanecoorie Reservoir currently at 1.62m and falling slowly, with minor flooding.
  • The Loddon River at Laanecoorie Reservoir may fall below the minor flood level (1.50m) overnight Saturday into Sunday.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Over-floor flooding of homes and buildings is not currently expected.
  • Lower areas of the Loddon floodplain may be flooded, including some minor roads.
  • Roads and bridges may be closed due to flooding. Check the VicTraffic website for road closures and follow instructions from emergency services.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 23/08/2026 01:00 pm or as the situation changes.

properties.webBody:
This is a Final Minor Flood Warning for the King River. 

Flooding is no longer estimated to be occuring at Docker Road Bridge.

Moderate rainfall across the King River catchment last week caused river levels to rise. Rainfall has now eased across the catchment. However, river levels remain elevated in response to the recent rainfall. 

Minor flooding is no longer estimated to be occurring along the King River at Docker Rd Bridge.

No observations are currently available for the King River at Docker Rd Bridge. The river level is estimated to have fallen below the minor flood level (3.70 m) early Saturday morning. The King River at Docker Rd Bridge will remain below the minor flood level (3.70 m).
The threat of flooding is reduced. Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and beware of hazards remaining in the warning area.
What you should do:
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
If your home or business has been flooded:
  • Check for building damage before you enter.
  • Have all electrical and gas equipment professionally tested before use.
  • Clean and dry out the building as soon as possible.
Call Triple Zero (000) in a life threatening emergency. For emergency assistance from the SES call 132 500.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Damage to roads and buildings caused by flooding may still exist in your area. 
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

This will be the last warning for this flood.

  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au

properties.name: Watch & Act
properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Avoca River to Charlton Town.

  • Rainfall early last week has resulted in another minor flood peak at Yawong Weir on Saturday morning.
  • This peak is likely to arrive at Charlton Town overnight Saturday into Sunday with moderate flooding. 
  • The Avoca River at Charlton Town is currently at 5.72m and rising, with minor flooding.
  • The Avoca River at Charlton Town is likely to peak near the moderate flood level (5.90m) overnight Saturday into Sunday.
Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Rising floodwater is dangerous. Drivers must be aware of water levels rising near you, especially overnight when visibility is poor.
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around and find a safe alternative route.
  • Never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:
  • Moderate flooding is likely along the Avoca River at Charlton Town and minor flooding is occurring at Yawong Weir.
  • Main roads, including the Calder Highway, could be closed due to flooding at any time. Drivers must follow diversions. For more information on road closures visit the VicTraffic website.
  • The Boort-Wycheproof Road crossing at the Avoca River may become flooded and unsafe to use.
  • Floodwater may affect Gordon Park Caravan Park.
  • Flooding of farmland downstream of Glenloth around Bunguluke and Ninyeunook, and inundation of local roads such as Jeruk River Road North and Ninyeunook Road, is possible.
  • Floodwaters may persist for several days as they move through the floodplain.
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Over-floor flooding of homes is not currently expected.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 23/08/2026 12:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility:

  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline.
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.name: Advice
properties.webBody:
This Advice is being issued for Guildford and Yapeen. 
  • This is an updated Advice message that replaces the message issued at 6:01pm on 20/08/2026.
  • Coliban Water has advised that as of Thursday 20 August, the tap water at Guildford and Yapeen is not safe to drink without boiling first. 
  • A burst water main occurred in Guildford late on Wednesday night.
  • This burst caused a supply interruption and low water pressure in both towns.
  • Low water pressure and interruptions to water supply can lead to a build-up of bacteria that can make people sick.
If you live or work within Guildford and Yapeen, you must boil tap water before drinking. 
What you should do:  
  • Boil water before drinking it, or drink bottled water.
  • Boil water for food preparation, cleaning fruit and vegetables, making ice and for preparing baby formula.
  • Boil water for brushing teeth. 
To ensure water is safe, you should: 
  • Heat water until a continuous and rapid stream of air-bubbles is produced from the bottom of a pan or kettle (kettles with automatic shut-off switches are suitable). 
  • Allow water to cool before use. 
  • Store water in a clean, closed container for later use. 
  • Be careful when boiling water to prevent scalding or burns.
  • If you are concerned that you may have been affected by contaminated water, contact your doctor or Nurse-on-Call. 
Impacts in your area: 
  • Coliban Water is working to restore drinking water in the town. You will not have tap water until it is restored.
  • Once water is restored, you need to boil it before drinking.
  • Drinking water can be sourced from:
  • John Powell Reserve, Midland Highway, Guildford.
  • 1 Templeton Street, Guildford, next to the old General Store.
  • Testing will need to occur once the water supply is back. This may take a few days.
This message was issued by Department of Health.

The next update is expected by 22/08/2026 06:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:

  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
